items.text: Supposeyou want to find the speed of carsdriving downyourroad.You may have seen thepoliceusing a mobile speed camera to check that drivers are keeping to the speed limit.Speed guns use microprocessors(computers on a chip')toproduce aninstant reading of the speed ofa movingvehicle,butyou can conductavery simple experiment to measure car speed.

items.label: text
items.text: Measure thedistancebetween twopointsalongastraightsection ofroadwith a tapemeasure or'click'wheel.Usea stopwatch tomeasure the time taken fora carto travel themeasured distance.Figure 1.4 showsyou how to operate your'speed trap'

items.text: Measure50mfroma startpoint along the sideof theroad.

items.label: list_item

items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: You can convert a speed in m/s into a speed inkm/h.

items.label: text
items.text: lf the cartravels12.8metres in one second itwill travel

items.label: text
items.text: 12.8x60 metresin 60 seconds (thatis, one minute)and

items.label: text
items.text: 12.8x60x60metresin60minutes (that is,1hour),which is

items.label: text
items.text: 46080metres inanhouror46.1km/h (to one decimal place).

items.label: text
items.text: We havemultipliedby3600(60x60)to convert from m/sto m/h,then divided by1000 toconvertfromm/h tokm/h （as there are 1000m in 1km）.

items.label: text
items.text: Rule:to convertm/s tokm/h simply multiply by 3.6.

items.label: text
items.text: Using the measurementsmade with your speed trap,you can work out the speed of the car.Use the equation:

items.label: text
items.text: distance moved,s average speed,v= time taken,t

items.label: text
items.text: So if the time measured is3.9 s,the speed of the carin this experiment is:

items.label: text
items.text: 50m average speed,v= 3.9s
